questions.question: The vertebrae are a part of which of the following body systems in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spinal cord.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Any animal having a backbone or Spinal cord is known as the **vertebrae** while invertebrates are animals that do not have a backbone.
 
• A total of** 33 vertebrae** are found in the vertebral column of humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vertical column is divided into the following regions: Thoracic, Cervical, Sacral, Coccygeal, and Lumbar.
 
• Thoracic:
 
 
• These are 12 in number ranging from T1 to T12.
 
• The rib cage is held by the thoracic spine and thus helps in protecting the lungs and heart as well.
 
 
 
• Cervical:
 
 
• There are 7 cervical vertebrae present in the neck region ranging from C1 to C7.
 
• The weight of the head is supported by these cervical vertebrae.
 
 
 
• Sacral:
 
 
• There are 5 sacral vertebrae found in the body's infused form.
 
• They help majorly in connecting the spine to the bones of the hip.
 
 
 
• Coccygeal:
 
 
• Their function is to provide attachment for muscles and ligaments in the pelvic floor.
 
• A total of four coccyx bones is present in the fused form.
 
 
 
• Lumbar:
 
 
• There is a presence of 5 lumbar vertebrae in the body ranging from L1 to L5.
 
• They function primarily in bearing the weight of the body.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the main causes of tides?

options.text: Gravitational pull of the Sun and the Moon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational pull of the Sun and the Moon.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Tides refer to the cyclic rise and fall of the seawater.
 
• The tides are caused by the** gravitational attraction of the moon and the sun** on the earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• The gravitational pull of the Moon causes high tides and low tides in the sea.
 
• The gravitational pull of the moon pulls the seas towards it, causing the ocean tides.
 
• Due to the difference in the gravitational force of the moon across the earth, there is also a bulge on the opposite side of the earth.

questions.question: Which of the following popular kitchen ingredients is called the 'sugar eating fungus'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yeast.**__

__
 
• Yeast is single-celled microorganisms that are classified, along with moulds and mushrooms, as members of the Kingdom Fungi.
 
• It is also known as **sugar eating fungus.**
 
 
• Yeasts are evolutionarily diverse and are therefore classified into two separate phyla, Ascomycota or sac fungi and Basidiomycota or higher fungi, that together form the subkingdom Dikarya.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Baking Powder - It is a dry chemical leavening agent, a mixture of a carbonate or bicarbonate, and a weak acid.

 
 
• These baking acids are tartrate, phosphate, and sodium aluminium sulfate used alone or in combination.
 
• It contains sodium bicarbonate.
 
 
 
• **Vinegar** is a sour liquid that is made by the fermentation of numerous dilute alcoholic liquids into a liquid containing acetic acid.
 
 
• Vinegar can be made from any liquid that is capable of being converted into alcohol in a two-step process.

questions.question: Which Mughal prince translated the Upanishads into Persian in 1657?

• Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads from Sanskrit to Persian so they could be read by Muslim scholars.
 
• His translation is often called Sirr-i-Akbar.
 
• Dara Shikoh was the eldest son and heir apparent of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• He devoted much effort towards finding a common mystical language between Islam and Hinduism.
 
• His spiritual quest for monotheistic strands in Hindu philosophy was a continuous process.
 
• This led him to study the Upanishads, with the help of some scholars of Benaras.
 
• This book was the greatest mystery and was completed in 1657.

• Abul Fazl wrote the Ain-i-Akbari and Akbar Nama.

questions.question: Payment made to others for the purchase of factors of production is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**explicit cost.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Explicit costs are expenses that are easily quantifiable and identifiable.
 
• Payment made to others for the purchase of factors of production is known as explicit cost.
 
• It includes direct payments/expenses in business like wages, rent, raw materials, etc.
 
• The explicit cost of capital can be referred to as the "discount rate" which equates the present value of cash inflow that is incremental of financing opportunity with the present value of cash outflows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Factors of production:__
 
• Land: 
 
 
• The land has a broad definition as a factor of production and can take on various forms, from agricultural land to commercial real estate to the resources available from a particular piece of land.
 
 
 
• Labor: 
 
 
• Labor refers to the effort expended by an individual to bring a product or service to the market. Again, it can take on various forms.
 
 
 
• Capital: 
 
 
• In economics, capital typically refers to money.
 
 
 
• Organization:
 
 
• A business organization is defined as a firm established and run to earn profit by producing and selling commodities.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the 'Pardoning Power of the Governor'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 161.**__

__
 
• **Article 161** of the Indian constitution deals with the Pardoning Power of the Governor.
 
• The Power of the Governor to grant** pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute** sentences in certain cases.
 
• The governor does not have the power to pardon the sentence inflicted by the **court-martial on the convict.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Pardoning Powers of the President -

 
 
• Pardon - It removes both the sentence and the conviction of the convict and completely absolves the convict from all sentences, punishments and disqualifications.
 
• Commutation - It substitutes one form of punishment for a lighter form. 
 
• Remission - It reduces the period of the sentence but the character of the sentence remains the same. 
 
• Respite - It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of one originally awarded due to some special fact such as the physical disability of a convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender, the President can use this power. 
 
• Reprieve - It implies a stay of the execution of a sentence (especially that of death) for a temporary period. Its purpose is to enable the convict to have time to seek pardon or commutation from the President.

questions.question: Melatonin encodes proteins in cells to prevent ______ entry
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

Key Points__**

__
 
• **Melatonin** encodes proteins in cells to prevent virus entry.

 
 
• Melatonin synthesised in the lungs acts as a barrier against **Covid-19 infection.**
 
• This also prevents the expression of genes that are entry points for the virus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Melatonin hormone is released by the Pineal gland

 
 
• The pineal gland is present on the dorsal side of the forebrain. It produces an enzyme called melatonin which is responsible for maintaining the diurnal rhythm (24-hour) of the body like the sleep-wake cycle, body temperature, etc.
 
• In addition, melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle as well as our defence capability.

questions.question: SIMBEX is a military exercise conducted between the defense forces of which of the following nations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and Singapore.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian Navy hosted the 27th edition of** India - Singapore Bilateral Maritime Exercise SIMBEX-20.**
 
• The SIMBEX series of exercises between the Indian Navy and Republic of Singapore Navy, being conducted annually** since 1994**, are aimed at enhancing mutual inter-operability and imbibing best practices from each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The joint military exercise between India and Thailand is **SITMEX.**

• Cope India (Air Force).
